_comment: The tracked egress inventory — every sanctioned OFF-DEVICE (or loopback-model) network call site, plus the pinned platform-security snapshot. scripts/check-security.mjs enforces it: a NEW ureq/fetch/network-CLI call site, a new HTTP-client crate, a keychain literal outside the named constants, or a widened CSP/capability/assetProtocol/updater field fails `check:security` until this file is deliberately updated. Adding a network call is a reviewed change (docs/development/security.md → 'Adding a network call'). Destination class + guard document WHY each site is safe; they are read by humans, not asserted byte-for-byte.

ureqFiles.web_search.rs: provider-dispatched search to literal DuckDuckGo lite/html or api.search.brave.com; query is secret/private-prose scanned and capped, redirects/body size/time are bounded, Brave auth comes from Keychain
ureqFiles.web.rs: web_fetch (arbitrary public web via the vetted_resolve SSRF-blocked agent, same-host redirects, byte+URL caps)
ureqFiles.chat.rs: the on-device model bridge — endpoint_permitted clamps the destination to registered loopback model servers; egress_allowed refuses protected transcripts to non-local endpoints
ureqFiles.breve.rs: breve_test_email — Resend send to the literal https://api.resend.com/emails host, Keychain Bearer, configured recipients only
ureqFiles.remote_agent.rs: explicit session connector to the user-entered HTTPS relay (loopback HTTP allowed in development); independent Keychain device/client credentials; redirects refused; request/response frames bounded; MCP responses come only from workspace.rs remote-policy handlers; vault switches fail closed unless disconnect succeeds; no frame logging
ureqFiles.antigravity.rs: antigravity_manage install — one pinned-hash download of Google's registry-listed ACP runtime from the literal https://dl.google.com archive URL (byte-capped stream, SHA-256 + size verified before extraction); no credential, no user content, off by default (ADR 2026-09-03)

gatedEgressSites._comment: Every Rust function that puts CALLER-SUPPLIED text on a network — a model transport, a CLI provider, or a web lane — must ask crate::secret::blocked_for_remote (the marker scan + the secure-prose ledger). Adding an outbound lane without the gate is the class the 2026-08-01 audit found three times: open_url had no content gate at all, the organizer's remote lane had none, and web_search had no size bound. check-security.mjs asserts each function below still calls the gate.

rawFetchFiles.safe-fetch.ts: the ONE hardened public-web reader (SSRF/redirect/cap guards) — the sanctioned raw fetch; every other web read must route through it
rawFetchFiles.llm.ts: local-model tier POSTs (generate / chat-completions / health / warmup) — llmConfig endpoint, loopback by policy (guarded by requireLocalEndpoint before every fetch)
rawFetchFiles.config.ts: no fetch — declared here only so a future edit that adds one is a conscious allowlist change
rawFetchFiles.summarize-url.ts: local-model /api/generate — LLM.endpoint (loopback tier); the page text it summarizes arrives via safe-fetch.ts
rawFetchFiles.watcher-check.ts: local-model /api/generate — LLM.endpoint (loopback tier); watched pages arrive via safe-fetch.ts
rawFetchFiles.signal-daemon.ts: local-model /api/generate lanes (loopback) + ONE host-pinned https://www.youtube.com/<handle> channel-resolve probe (literal host, interpolation steers the PATH only, checkUrl-gated)
rawFetchFiles.creator-alerts.ts: host-pinned https://www.youtube.com/feeds/videos.xml RSS poll (literal host, channelId steers the query only)
rawFetchFiles.auth.ts: Resend send — literal https://api.resend.com/emails, Keychain Bearer
rawFetchFiles.email-topic.ts: Resend send — literal https://api.resend.com/emails, Keychain Bearer
rawFetchFiles.send-brief.ts: Resend send — literal https://api.resend.com/emails, Keychain Bearer

imapFlowFiles.mail.ts: ImapFlow client.fetch — configured mail hosts, TLS strict except loopback; not a raw fetch

src._comment: Webview app code. connect-src is ipc-only, so a raw fetch( here cannot reach the network or the asset protocol; vault bytes ride corpusFileBytes. Declare a call site only with a documented reason.

rawFetchFiles.src/lib/helperClient.ts: Rotli Web only: GET /health and POST /rpc to http://127.0.0.1:<port> — Rotli Helper on the user's own computer, bearer token from the pairing code. Never reachable in the Mac app (ipc-only connect-src); the site's /app/ policy opens connect-src to loopback alone (site/Caddyfile).

keychain._comment: The allowlisted account names may appear ONLY at their named-constant declaration sites + the parity fixture + tests. Any other literal occurrence fails the check — callers must import the constant.

tauriConf._comment: Snapshot of the security-load-bearing tauri.conf.json fields. Widening any of these (a remote connect-src/img-src host, a second updater endpoint, a broader assetProtocol scope) fails the check until this snapshot is deliberately updated in the same change.
tauriConf.csp: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' asset: http://asset.localhost blob: data:; font-src 'self' data:; media-src 'self' asset: http://asset.localhost blob: data:; frame-src 'self' asset: http://asset.localhost; connect-src ipc: http://ipc.localhost
tauriConf.devCsp: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' asset: http://asset.localhost blob: data:; font-src 'self' data:; media-src 'self' asset: http://asset.localhost blob: data:; frame-src 'self' asset: http://asset.localhost; connect-src ipc: http://ipc.localhost ws://localhost:1420 http://localhost:1420

capabilities._comment: The default capability's granted permissions and exact app-owned webview targets. A new fs/shell/http plugin permission or window-wide target (which would grant a private-browser child IPC) fails until pinned here.

sensitiveLogging._comment: Heuristic (documented limits in docs/development/security.md): flags a println!/eprintln!/console.log in an egress-adjacent file whose argument names a body/secret/prompt/transcript variable. It catches the obvious regression (logging a note body next to a network call); it CANNOT prove the absence of a leak — a renamed variable or an interpolated helper slips it. It is a tripwire, not a proof.
